A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DOLPHIN and retain matching methods and experiments. All pages, including v1's appendices A–B and v2's appendices A–H, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original training times, benchmark accuracies, provenance ablations, and Mugen convergence curves in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports the retained benchmark experiments plus original LTN comparisons, HWF execution-time measurements, and MNIST ProductN experiments.

M1.justification: Table 1 revises the reported DTKP-AM zero/unit tag initialization. V1 gives zero a positive-infinity first row and makes the unit entirely positive infinity; v2 makes zero entirely negative infinity and represents the unit with one empty proof. This is a limited provenance-component correction. The five primitives, training objective, and overall framework remain; expanded execution and recursion explanations do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: The original five task families and their benchmark variants remain, with Small/Medium/Large renamed using explicit sizes. V2 Appendix G adds MNIST ProductN for N = 4, 8, 16, and 20, introducing multiplication requirements beyond the existing digit-summation task.

E2.justification: V2 adds Logic Tensor Networks as an evaluated comparator on SumN: Table 3 reports 92.54 seconds for SumN-5 and out-of-memory outcomes for SumN-10/15. Scallop, ISED, and IndeCateR+ retain their previous comparison coverage. Discussion of other frameworks does not establish additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 makes total-time speedup the main comparison, replacing v1's per-epoch ratio while retaining per-epoch comparisons in Appendix D. PathFinder's stated top-k changes from 3 to 1. New protocols compare sequential CPU execution with GPU tag computation for HWF and batch sizes 64 versus 256 for ProductN. The main data splits and ten-hour timeout remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained provenance ablation and Mugen convergence analysis, v2 Appendix B isolates HWF's CPU user-function and tag-computation costs, comparing sequential and parallelized execution. Appendix G tests combinatorial scaling and batch-size sensitivity using ProductN. These directly investigate the mechanisms and limits underlying scalability.

E5.justification: Both versions report three trials and average best accuracy and training time. Error bars already appear in v1's accuracy and provenance figures and remain in v2. No new seed policy, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Many reported results change. DOLPHIN's SumN-5 total time changes from 78.33 to 53.86 seconds; IndeCateR+ on SumN-15 changes from a timeout in v1 Table 2 to 548.28 seconds in v2 Table 3. IndeCateR+ accuracy bars also change substantially in Figure 5. V2 adds LTN, HWF timing-breakdown, and ProductN outcomes. PathFinder's revised results accompany its changed top-k setting.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix A adds an upper-bound argument for the add-mult WMC approximation and a dependent-input equality counterexample: DAMP yields a sum of squared probabilities, whereas DTKP-AM yields probability one when the distribution has at most k symbols. It also explains absent-symbol/proof representations. Table 1 revises zero/unit definitions, and the DAMP prose corrects the previously reversed conjunction/disjunction operations.

C1.justification: V1 broadly presents symbolic forward chaining and the computation graph as GPU-vectorized. V2's abstract and introduction explicitly place symbolic manipulation on CPU and neural/probabilistic computation on GPU, materially narrowing the acceleration claim. The headline efficiency claim changes from 0.33%–37.17% of baseline training time to 1.71x–62x faster convergence on simpler benchmarks, while retaining the claim of scalability on harder cases.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of overlapping-proof double counting, preserved top-k semantics, remaining combinatorial growth, and unsupported nondeterministic symbolic programs. Appendix D.7 newly hypothesizes that backend autodifferentiation differences explain Mugen convergence, explicitly marking this explanation as unconfirmed. These extend v1's limitations concerning batched programming and unexplored generative-model support.

D1.justification: V2 adds detailed HWF neural/symbolic code, recursion examples, tensor-storage and execution details, and richer PathFinder, CLUTRR, and Mugen implementation descriptions beyond v1's existing hyperparameter appendix. Its main hardware description now agrees with v1's RTX 2080 Ti appendix disclosure. Conversely, v1's statement that framework and benchmark code are supplied in supplementary material disappears without replacement access instructions.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against GPU tensor-based frameworks, including LYRICS, LTN, and TensorLog, discussing their grounding requirements and expressivity in the introduction, Section 5, and Appendices F/H. It also adds discussion of probabilistic-circuit and variable-elimination work and specialized recurrent models. This broadens v1's emphasis on CPU-based frameworks and proof-search optimizations.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around CLUTRR and the CPU/GPU division. The overview and framework exposition are condensed and reorganized, benchmark names become explicit sizes, and existing experimental details and convergence discussion are integrated into a substantially reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is replaced by a CLUTRR illustration; the original SumN component diagram moves to Appendix D. V1 Table 2 is reorganized into v2 Tables 2, 3, and 5. The provenance plots move to Figure 10 with a logarithmic timing axis, and new timing-breakdown and ProductN tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the scalability argument by clarifying CPU/GPU responsibilities, adding an evaluated GPU-based comparator, and directly measuring execution costs and combinatorial scaling. The approximation analysis and implementation details also make the contribution more assessable. These gains outweigh localized new defects: Table 5's SumN-5 Scallop ratio is 3.43 although 184.76/10.77 is approximately 17.15, and the HWF listing contains incomplete conditions. Those errors still limit numerical reliability and reproducibility.
